identity: Writer and women's rights activist · France · 1804–1876
title: George Sand's birth chart
metaDescription: George Sand's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 9.3° Cancer. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.3° separates the Sun and Pluto from an exact trine; at that range identity and depth read as one mechanism. A trine is an open channel. The two cooperate without being asked, which is exactly why it is easy to spend and easy to take for granted.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 9.3° Cancer, inside the first decan (0°–10°), whose traditional sub-ruler is the Moon. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Mercury holds 18.1° Gemini, Venus holds 17.1° Leo, Mars holds 22.6° Taurus — in the old shorthand, thought that travels by comparison; attraction declared rather than implied; effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: the Sun to Pluto, a trine with 0.3° of slack. The scheme reads trines as water finding its level: effortless, and invisible to the person living it. Behind it, Mars opposition Neptune at 0.8°, and Mercury sextile Venus at 1.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Mars opposes Neptune while both square Venus. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, two placements stand out. Mercury in Gemini at 18.1° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mars in Taurus at 22.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 3 water, 3 air, 2 fire, 2 earth by element and 4 cardinal, 3 mutable, 3 fixed by mode. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Aries for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.2° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 20.4°.
